messages:
Maya: Hey team — need to lock down a customer spotlight with Aurora Labs for next Wed launch post + companion webinar. They asked for a 20min on-camera interview and one short publishable quote. Can someone coordinate scheduling, draft interview Qs, and flag any legal concerns? Also need high-res logo and headshot from the customer.

Devon: I can run the interview. Available Mon/Tue mornings PST. Will take notes and pull a draft quote after the call.

Ben: I'll intro to their head of ML and request headshot/logo + usage numbers. Can also surface a metric we can use (latency reduction on batch scoring).

Maya: Draft Qs (quick list):
```
- Quick product/context: what problem were you solving?
- Workflow: how are you using Redwood in prod?
- Impact: any quantitative wins (cost, latency, throughput)?
- Decision: why Redwood vs alternatives?
- Advice: anything you'd tell other infra teams evaluating inference?
```
Plan is to keep it tight — 6 Qs + time for a live demo clip.

Alex: Heads-up — marketing copy should avoid absolute claims ("instant", "99% faster") without a citation. Carmen, can legal review the proposed quote phrasing?

Carmen: Yep — ask the customer for approval on the exact quote text and provide evidence for quantitative claims. We prefer the quote in a Google Doc so we can track redlines. Also need a signed release for the recording.

Sam: I can produce the hero graphic + social card. Need a vector logo and a ~3000x2000 headshot. Ben, can you get those in the next 48h?

Ben: On it. Pinged Aurora legal for asset consent and a headshot. ETA 24–48h.

Devon: After the interview I'll post a short write-up + one suggested quote. Drafting a potential quote now for early review:
`\"Redwood reduced our end-to-end inference latency and stabilized throughput for peak loads, letting us ship higher-value features faster.\"`

Carmen: Edit suggestion — remove "reduced our end-to-end inference latency" unless you can give a specific baseline + delta. Maybe: `\"Redwood stabilized throughput under peak loads and improved latency for critical paths, helping us ship higher-value features faster.\"` Also: customer must approve verbatim.

Maya: Good call. Devon — please include the alternate phrasing. After the customer signs off we can request Legal's final sign-off and then route to approvals-bot for publish queue.

Devon: Will do. Tentative interview Monday 9am PST. I'll drop calendar invites and the doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/aurora-spotlight-draft (internal).

approvals-bot: Approval requested: marketing/customer-spotlights — awaiting legal and customer sign-off.

Alex: Quick note on messaging: emphasize deployment flexibility (hosted -> private) in the byline; helps with enterprise readers.

Maya: Thanks all — timeline: interview Mon, draft quote by Tue EOD, customer sign-off Wed morning, publish prep Wed afternoon. Carmen — once customer signs, can you confirm legal sign-off so approvals-bot can move it to publish? :thumbsup:

Carmen: Will confirm after I see the signed quote/release. If Aurora signs off by Wed AM we can clear legal same day.

Ben: Aurora confirmed the headshot and logo just now, and will review the quote after the interview. Sharing assets in #secure-assets shortly.

Maya: Perfect — I'll start the launch checklist and assign social copy + webinar ops after the quote is final. Thanks team :party_parrot:

Devon: Note for post: let's capture a 60s customer clip for the webinar trailer.

Sam: Noted — I'll prep an export template for the clip so it's social-ready.

approvals-bot: Status update: waiting_on -> legal, customer_signoff."
